identity.name: Fen Vikutā
identity.bio: An Arasaka researcher raised in Japan, born to a Japanese researcher and a Night City-born intelligence operative. Both parents were Saburo loyalists. Fen carries their legacy into a life stripped of corporate protection. An autodidact with a taste for older films and Japanese sports cars, he spent years driving and drifting in Japan and Night City.

attributes.description: Initiative, evasion, stealth and ranged weapon handling.

proficiencies.tools_note: Cybertech kit proficient; kit not owned.

resources.hp_note: Full fighting condition. No critical injuries.
resources.rest_note: Two Tier-1 Execution Slots return after a Short Rest or Long Rest. A qualifying fed and hydrated Long Rest restores full HP.

programs.name: Short Circuit
programs.summary: Overload exposed circuitry with a precise destructive packet.
programs.effect: Make one ranged program attack (+6) against a visible compatible powered target. On a hit, deal 1d10 + 3 Electrical damage to physical HP, or 1d10 + 3 Data damage to ICE integrity in software mode. At total levels 5, 11 and 17, send 2, 3 and 4 packets respectively, each with its own attack and target. Output Amplifier adds Cool (+3) to every hit, included above.
programs.requirements: Wirelessly target powered Cyberware or an electronic actor/object within range; its circuitry supplies the destructive current. Software mode targets reachable ICE and uses virtual AC. Declare each packet’s mode before attacking.
programs.scaling: At character levels 5, 11 and 17, send 2, 3 and 4 packets respectively. Output Amplifier adds Cool to every hit.

programs.name: Decoy Projection
programs.summary: Spoof an image or sound in electronic senses or nearby presentation hardware.
programs.effect: Create one sound, from a whisper to a scream, or a static object image within a 5-foot cube. An image adds no sound, smell, light or solidity. Physical interaction reveals an image. A creature examining it with an action can identify the deception with Intelligence (Investigation) DC 14. Ends on dismissal (action), replacement by another execution or after 1 minute.
programs.requirements: Use reachable electronic sensory feeds within 60 feet of the effect, or an actual speaker/display/projector able to produce it physically. Feed-only illusions affect compatible electronic observers; ordinary eyes and offline sensors are unaffected.
programs.scaling: Utility; no slot and no level-based increase.

programs.name: Vulnerability Tag
programs.summary: Mark a neural weakness and exploit it with each successful attack.
programs.effect: Choose a visible reachable neural or robotic target; no initial save. Your attacks against it deal an extra 1d6 damage matching the triggering attack’s primary damage type on a hit. Choose one ability: its checks have disadvantage, not its Saving Throws. After it reaches 0 HP, transfer the tag to another legal target with a Bonus Action on a subsequent turn. A software-target mode can mark reachable ICE; the rider on a Data attack deals Data damage. For mixed attacks, the direct base damage is primary; if the base is mixed, use its first printed component.
programs.requirements: Wirelessly target integrated neural Cyberware or a robotic system within range. Software mode targets a reachable ICE instance. Maintain Concentration for the printed duration.
programs.scaling: Tier 3–4: up to 8 hours. Tier 5+: up to 24 hours. Tier 2: still 1 hour. Firmware clearance can end it.

programs.name: Neural Seizure
programs.summary: Disrupt neural and motor control, dropping a target into incapacitating spasms.
programs.effect: Choose one visible compatible target within range with Intelligence 5 or higher. It makes a Cool Saving Throw against DC 14. On failure, it falls Prone and is Incapacitated and unable to stand for the duration. At the end of each of its turns and whenever it takes damage, it repeats the save, with advantage if damage triggered that save. A success ends the Program. Incapacitated creatures cannot take Actions or Reactions, including Bonus Actions, and lose Concentration.
programs.requirements: Wireless upload to compatible neural or motor-control Cyberware within range; no preliminary breach check. Spend one Execution Slot and maintain Concentration.

programs.name: Overheat
programs.summary: Overload powered Cyberware to generate damaging heat.
programs.effect: One powered synthetic or living target with substantial powered Cyberware makes a Constitution Saving Throw against DC 14. On failure, it takes 2d6 Thermal damage immediately and 1d6 at the end of each of its turns, starting with its next turn. After each recurring damage instance, repeat the save; success ends the Program. Initial success negates the Program. The target can use an Action to shut down the addressed system and end the Program, losing that system’s benefit until it uses an Action to restart it.
programs.requirements: Wireless upload to a compatible powered target within range. Spend one Execution Slot and maintain Concentration. Heat comes from the addressed Cyberware; cannot address life support or fabricate fuel.
programs.scaling: Each Tier above 1 adds 1d6 to initial damage only.

features.name: Burst Processing
features.detail: Cool is your program ability. Attack +6; save DC 14. Known software is fixed between levels. Two tier-1 slots return on a Short Rest or Long Rest. Utilities consume no slot. One Concentration program at a time; on damage make a Constitution save (+2), DC 10 or half damage, whichever is higher. If you execute a Bonus Action Program, every other Program on that turn must be a Utility with an execution time of one Action. This restriction applies in either order. All programs need their real equipment and access.

features.name: Semantic Link
features.summary: Silent translated messages · 30 ft · At Will
features.detail: Send one-way messages wirelessly to a visible recipient through compatible neural Cyberware or a communication endpoint within 30 feet. The recipient must understand at least one language; you do not need to share it. No Execution Slot is spent. The link carries your message, not the recipient’s thoughts.

features.name: Research Network
features.summary: Find the likely archive, department or specialist for a technical question
features.detail: You know how to identify the likely department or archive for a technical question and how to request access. Credentials, trust, time and actual access still matter. Former employment does not restore revoked permissions.

features.name: Output Amplifier
features.summary: Firmware Upgrade · +3 damage per Short Circuit hit
features.detail: Add your Cool modifier (+3) to every Short Circuit hit, including its Electrical and Data modes. Passive; no Action, Execution Slot or additional Load.

features.name: Social Engineering
features.detail: Gain proficiency in Deception and Persuasion. Each currently uses Cool +3 and Proficiency Bonus +2, for +5. Existing proficiency is not doubled. Passive; no Action, Execution Slot or additional Load.

cyberware.name: Cyclops Civic C2
cyberware.summary: Cyan iris shells · Chyron HUD · two empty option slots per eye
cyberware.detail: Cyclops International Civic C2 replacement eyes, a second-hand matched pair fitted by Maelstrom. Human-shaped housings with cyan iris shells provide ordinary vision and a built-in Chyron HUD. Each eye has two empty optical option slots. Persistent advertising crowds the display, imposing disadvantage on sight-based Perception until replacement. Passive Perception: sight 7 (12 minus 5 for disadvantage); other senses 12.

cyberware.name: Rocklin Augmentics NP-1
cyberware.summary: Exposed ear-mounted controller; basic interface functions only
cyberware.detail: Decades-old Rocklin cyberware patched together by Maelstrom. A bulky external casing hooks around the right ear, connected to an implanted neural anchor. Two exposed adapter sockets accept shards; one holds the Ronin Fragment and one is empty; a basic personal-link lead exits beside the upper-neck mount. Fen conceals the casing beneath his hair. When the distinctive casing is visible, observers have advantage on Perception checks to recognise or identify Fen using it as an identifying feature. Concealing it beneath his hair removes that visual cue. Exposed connections are vulnerable to snagging, grabbing or direct damage. Retains a biomonitor, basic HUD, neural link, virtuality display and five empty neuralware option connections.

cyberware.name: Ronin Fragment
cyberware.summary: Arasaka Shadow Mk.1 Cyberdeck running Ronin’s local Fragment
cyberware.detail: An Arasaka Shadow Mk.1 Cyberdeck loaded with Ronin’s bounded local Fragment, connected through the NP-1 neural interface. Slim black casing, translucent red circuitry cover and white Arasaka markings. The Fragment replaces the corporate firmware, disabling Arasaka telemetry, remote administration and manufacturer backdoors. Occupies one shard socket while slotted. While operating, multiplies native Neural Tolerance by 1.2, rounded down before earned Adaptation and lasting Tolerance Injury: 11 → 13, and grants +1 to Contractor Program attack rolls and Program Save DC, including Utilities: Attack +6, DC 14 at current attributes. Supplies the Contractor interface locally; these passive benefits require no extra charge or Execution Slot. Removal ends these bonuses; recalculate Tolerance, Overload and the Stability ceiling under the normal rules. A makeshift Agent function added during the jailbreak supports calls to and from Ronin only.

finances.housing: Sunset Motel, Room 12 prepaid through 19 November, 22:00. Authorised occupant of Mori’s Unit Four workshop in Rancho Coronado. Corporate housing revoked.

journal.title: Fen Vikutā
journal.body: Raised in Japan. Former Arasaka researcher specialising in engram modelling, cognitive systems and laboratory software.

journal.title: Behind the wheel
journal.body:
Years of serious driving and drifting in Japan and Night City made Fen an exceptional driver. His family’s influence protected him from much routine traffic enforcement; in Night City, corporate connections and occasional bribes helped.

His former car was a pearl-white Mizutani Shion MZ2 with dark graphite wheels, a carefully maintained interior, adjustable suspension, a limited-slip differential and upgraded brakes. Arasaka seized it with his corporate housing. Its whereabouts are unknown.

journal.title: Roadside
journal.body: After the raid, blindness and a Maelstrom abduction, Fen wakes in a roadside carpark. His vision has returned through unfamiliar, advert-cluttered optics. A public telephone is ringing.

journal.title: The Fragment
journal.body: In Sunset Motel room 12, Fen checks the Tamayura and installs Ronin’s runtime shard. His programs come online.

journal.title: Morning
journal.body: After eating, washing and sleeping, Fen wakes in Room 12 to the telephone ringing at nine.

journal.title: A change of clothes
journal.body: Bought a plain jacket outfit at Second Shift and discarded the old Arasaka clothing in an alley dumpster.

journal.title: Mesa Industrial Surplus
journal.body:
Nolan quoted €$5,500 for both R-440 compute servers and the S-120 storage server, including replacement of its faulty fan. Sale quote valid until 19 November, 11:47, while stock remains available.

Alternatively, one R-440 rents for €$250 per 30 days with a €$1,000 refundable deposit: €$1,250 upfront. Rental quote valid until 19 November, 11:58. No hosting offered. Written quotes sent to Mori; no equipment acquired.

Both quotes have now expired unaccepted. Ronin has deferred the purchase; availability and terms need reconfirmation.

journal.title: Switchyard Repairs — completed
journal.body: Recovered the recorder’s full 48 hours of delivery records for Vera Sanz, including an unscheduled stop followed by a damaged-shipment entry. Payment received: €$600. Earned 150 XP.

journal.title: Cinder Court — Unit Four
journal.body:
Mori secured the workshop lease. Fen holds the personnel-door and shutter keys and is authorised to stay overnight. The workshop was empty on handover. Servers and cooling have not been installed; supplies and bedding were brought in the following day.

Monthly rent: €$900, paid through 18 December, 18:50. Half the security deposit is paid; the remaining €$450 is due 2 December, 18:50. Water, sewer and the existing connection are included; electricity is metered separately. Cooling installation needs Ortega’s approval of specifications and placement.

journal.title: Street purchases
journal.body: Bought a refurbished Zetatech Grade A Agent, Shinsei Red cigarettes and a lighter. Rancho Arms supplied a fitted Tamayura holster, an empty spare magazine and 50 standard-ball cartridges.

journal.title: Morning at the motel
journal.body: After returning by taxi, eating and speaking with Ronin about software and neural-interface work, Fen showered and slept. At 07:00, the new Agent rang before breakfast.

journal.title: Supplies at Unit Four
journal.body: Brought the remaining meals and water from Sunset Motel to Unit Four by taxi. Fare paid: €$60. Relay Cybernetics is about half an hour away on foot; Ronin was awaiting a reply to his inquiry at the time.

journal.title: Relay Cybernetics — completed
journal.body:
Corrected the cyberarm adapter acknowledgement profile and passed bench tests. Dr Patricia Cárdenas paid €$450. Earned 50 XP.

Fen shared his Agent number, saved as Vik, and browsed the clinic’s new and refurbished cyberware. No implant purchased. Future fault reports and bookings go through Mori; no further clinic job agreed.

journal.title: Next work
journal.body: Ronin renewed his existing hosting for another week and deferred Nolan’s servers. He proposed seeking a fixer introduction for retrieval work using Fen’s technical skills.

journal.title: Kevlar vest
journal.body: Purchased a new black Kevlar vest from Rancho Arms for €$200, fitted beneath the jacket. Armour Class is now 13.

journal.title: Bedding for Unit Four
journal.body: Bought a folding cot, two fleece blankets and a pillow with pillowcase from Valley Home & Surplus for €$140. Carried everything back to Unit Four.

journal.title: Settling in
journal.body: Ate one meal, drank a litre of water and set up the cot, both blankets and pillow in Unit Four’s rear room. Two sealed meals and 2.5 litres of water remain here. Ronin’s deck call is still open.

journal.title: Back to Switchyard
journal.body: Slept for an hour on the cot, locked Unit Four and bought a chilli-cheese dog and energy drink for €$16. Ate and drank on the walk, then smoked one cigarette. Met Vera early to discuss field retrieval work. Stored supplies unchanged.

journal.title: Switchyard Repairs — meeting
journal.body: Attended Vera’s meeting early to discuss retrieval work. The resulting Cairn Instruments recovery was subsequently completed.

journal.title: Coldwater Recovery
journal.body: Accepted the inspection plan with Inez Barreto. Received a €$250 advance and Cairn’s loan diagnostic kit. Inez drove to the Arroyo yard. Arturo demonstrated the controller’s incomplete startup; Fen began inspecting the rig; the completed recovery is recorded below.

journal.title: Cairn Instruments — recovery completed
journal.body: Verified and recovered CI-146 from Coldwater without gunfire. Returned the rig and loan service kit to Vera at Switchyard. Remaining €$750 received; earned 150 XP, reaching level 2. Selected Output Amplifier, Social Engineering and Overheat.

rules.rests: Short Rest: 1 hour, restores Contractor slots. Long Rest: 8 hours under the normal 2014 requirements, once per 24 hours; begin with at least 1 HP. Restores class resources and half total Hit Dice, minimum 1. With adequate food and water, restores full HP to your effective maximum. Injuries and their penalties persist; exhaustion follows its separate recovery rule.
rules.convalescence: Once per 24 hours, after 8 hours of rest with food, water and appropriate first aid, spend up to one quarter of total Hit Dice rounded up (half in a stocked clinic). At level 2 this is one d8 + 2, minimum 0 HP. Critical injuries must be treated first. The same eight hours can qualify for a Long Rest; do not spend Hit Dice if it already restored full HP. Medical convalescence remains available when a Long Rest does not qualify. HP recovery leaves injury penalties and recovery clocks intact.
rules.injuries: The first damaging drop from positive HP to 0 in an encounter causes one critical injury. A critical hit above 0 does not. Standard injuries require treatment and 7 qualifying convalescence days; major injuries associated with a failed death save require surgery and 21 days.
rules.intrusion: Quickhacks upload wirelessly within their printed range. Target identification and upload are part of execution; resolve the Program’s attack or Saving Throw. Utilities are at will; tiered Programs spend an Execution Slot. Effects need a physical source: powered Cyberware for an overload, fuel and ignition for a combustion blast, or a chemical payload for toxins. Ordinary use of owned equipment costs no Execution Slot. A Program adds its printed intrusion, automation or enhancement; a separate implant named after every Program is not required.
rules.capacity: Native Neural Tolerance = max(4, 6 + Constitution modifier + Cool modifier) = 11. Add earned Adaptation, currently 0. Current Load: 0. Load above tolerance creates overload risk. Baseline replacements are Load 0. Operating Ronin Fragment multiplies native Tolerance by 1.2, rounded down: floor(11 × 1.2) = 13. Add Adaptation, then subtract lasting Tolerance Injury, to a minimum Tolerance of 1. Upgraded Fragments replace the existing multiplier rather than stacking.
rules.progression: Level 2: two Tier-1 slots and three known Programs. Firmware Upgrades: Output Amplifier and Social Engineering. Known Programs: Vulnerability Tag, Neural Seizure and Overheat. Level 3 at 900 total XP: Interface Platform and Tier-2 slots. On level advancement: new HP = floor(previous HP × new maximum / previous maximum). Full HP remains full; zero remains zero. Other resources are not replenished.
rules.secured_intrusion: Use Intelligence (Technology), currently +4, for meaningful obstacles such as protected files or persistent access. Routine work needs no roll; complex jobs can involve several distinct checks. This costs no Execution Slot. Active opposition can instead become a deep-dive combat encounter using normal initiative, actions, attacks and saves, with suitable deep-dive equipment.
rules.weapon_handling: Arasaka Tamayura: semiautomatic Power pistol. Each attack spends one round. Detachable magazine reload: Action or Bonus Action with a free hand, once per turn, using an accessible compatible magazine. Magazine capacity 8; current load 7 in the magazine + 1 chambered. One empty standard 8-round spare magazine and 50 boxed matching cartridges owned. Total ammunition: 58, including 8 loaded.
rules.cyberware_overrides:
### Voluntary Override
An eligible implant can exceed a physiological recovery limit or safety governor. It uses its normal activation, prerequisites and duration, and supplies one activation. Each override costs 1 Stability, followed by a Cool save; success prevents further loss, while failure loses another 1, or 2 on failure by 5 or more, with the normal symptom procedure.

### Escalating Risk
One shared counter covers every implant. Each earlier override since the last qualifying Long Rest adds +2 to the next override save DC, after the normal DC cap. Every override requires its save. A coincident ordinary trigger combines into that check. A qualifying Long Rest resets the counter; Stability recovers only through its separate recovery and treatment rules.

### Eligibility
The equipment card specifies override eligibility. This bypasses a physiological or governor limit; it cannot refill Execution Slots, ammunition, injectors or air reserves, or repair broken hardware. Ordinary permitted use has no override cost. First reaching zero Stability cannot itself trigger lasting Tolerance Injury; the existing catastrophic-breakdown procedure still governs that risk.

### Relative Acceleration
Sandevistan models specify normal and maximum overclock ratings. For physical weapon or unarmed attacks, a faster attacker has advantage against a slower target; a slower attacker has disadvantage. Equal ratings confer neither. Normal advantage cancellation, cover and targeting apply.

### Overclock
A supported overclock lasts until the start of your next ordinary turn, or until the implant ends. Each interval costs one override. Exceeding the safe-use allowance and overclocking the same activation count as one combined override. Each model defines its actual limits and activation timing.

### Accelerated Turn
A high-end model may grant one extra turn immediately after your ordinary turn, at most once per round: movement, an Action, an eligible Bonus Action and the normal object interaction. Extra Attack and eligible once-per-turn offensive features work normally. Resources, ammunition, Concentration and per-turn Program restrictions still apply.

### Timing
Only ordinary turns advance ongoing damage or healing, cooldowns, condition expiry, death saves, scheduled recovery saves and Reaction refresh. Movement, attacks and other actual events still trigger their normal effects during accelerated activity. Extra turns cannot generate more accelerated turns; once-per-round features stay once per round.

### Model Specifications
Duration, safe uses, ratings, movement, Load and combinations belong to each model’s equipment card. The existing R3 reflex accelerator retains its listed effects. No Sandevistan is currently installed.
